svg.font-family: 'Avenir Next', Avenir, 'Helvetica Neue', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Assisted is not the same as learned
svg.desc: Results from a high school mathematics experiment with nearly 1,000 students. While using the tool during practice sessions, students with ordinary GPT-4 improved grades by 48 percent and students with a teacher-designed guarded tutor improved by 127 percent. On a later unassisted exam with the tool removed, the ordinary GPT-4 group performed 17 percent worse than students who never had access, while the guarded-tutor group was statistically indistinguishable from the control group: the harm was prevented, but no learning gain appeared.
svg.text: Assisted is not the same as learned.
Nearly 1,000 high-school mathematics students, measured twice: with the tool, then without it.
WHILE USING THE TOOL · PRACTICE SESSIONS
AFTER IT WAS TAKEN AWAY · UNASSISTED EXAM
Better grades while the tool was in hand.
Worse than the students who never
An even larger gain during practice.
The harm was prevented. No learning gain appeared.
Assisted performance was not the same thing as learning.
Guardrails designed by teachers prevented the damage; they did not by themselves create understanding. Source: Bastani et al.,
“Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics,” PNAS, 2025.
